## Simulation

The library depends on the weather only, so the solution is a cumulative sum:

```r
simulate <- function(xi, Theta_y, y0) {
  increments <- Theta_y[-nrow(Theta_y), , drop = FALSE] %*% t(xi)
  sweep(rbind(0, apply(increments, 2, cumsum)), 2, y0, "+")   # day x genotype
}
```

The model is fitted to all seasons except 1998 (shared support of 12 terms, plus genotype deviations) and used to predict 1998 from its weather. All 199 genotypes are shown.

## Leave-one-year-out cross-validation

The same procedure is repeated for each of the 31 seasons.

```r
cv_blocked <- function(Theta, tr, gram, fitter = fit_ssr, k = 12,
                       lam_mu = 1e-4, lam_g = 0.01, ...) {
  ny <- length(tr$years)
  P <- array(NA_real_, c(dim(tr$Y)[1], ny, dim(Theta)[2]))
  support <- vector("list", ny)
  for (v in seq_len(ny)) {
    train <- setdiff(seq_len(ny), v)
    f <- fit_years(gram, train, fitter, k, lam_mu, lam_g, ...)
    y0 <- rowMeans(tr$Y[, train, 1])
    P[, v, ] <- t(simulate(f$xi, Theta[v, , ], y0))
    support[[v]] <- f$support
  }
  list(pred = P, support = support)
}
```

```r
evaluate <- function(P, tr, fixed_day = 99) {
  sq_error <- 0
  count <- 0
  final <- numeric(0)
  for (g in seq_len(dim(P)[1])) {
    for (y in seq_len(dim(P)[2])) {
      n <- tr$nend[g, y]
      d <- 2:(n + 1)                    # index 1 is the given initial value
      sq_error <- sq_error + sum((P[g, y, d] - tr$Y[g, y, d])^2)
      count <- count + n
      final <- c(final, P[g, y, n + 1] - tr$Y[g, y, n + 1])
    }
  }
  fixed <- (P[, , fixed_day] - tr$Y[, , fixed_day])^2
  c(trajectory_rmse = sqrt(sq_error / count),
    fixed_day_rmse = sqrt(mean(fixed, na.rm = TRUE)),
    maturity_rmse = sqrt(mean(final^2)))
}
```

## Baseline without weather

As a reference, each trajectory is predicted by the mean curve of the same genotype in the other seasons.

```r
lookup_trajectory <- function(tr) {
  hold_last <- function(v) replace(v, is.nan(v), tail(v[!is.nan(v)], 1))
  P <- array(NA_real_, dim(tr$Y))
  for (y in seq_along(tr$years)) {
    m <- apply(tr$Y[, -y, , drop = FALSE], c(1, 3), mean, na.rm = TRUE)
    P[, y, ] <- t(apply(m, 1, hold_last))
    P[, y, 1] <- tr$Y[, y, 1]
  }
  P
}
```


::: {.cell}

round(evaluate(base, tr), 3)

## Choice of fitting method

All methods share the signature `fit(A, b, ...)`, so they can be compared in one loop.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
methods <- list(OLS = list(fitter = fit_ols),
                ridge = list(fitter = fit_ridge, lambda = 0.01),
                SSR_8 = list(fitter = fit_ssr, k = 8),
                SSR_12 = list(fitter = fit_ssr, k = 12),
                lasso = list(fitter = fit_lasso, lambda = 2e-4))

compare <- function(m) {
  cv <- do.call(cv_blocked, c(list(Theta, tr, gram), m))
  round(evaluate(cv$pred, tr), 3)
}
res <- cached("swap_methods.rds", {
  scores <- t(sapply(methods, compare))
  data.frame(method = names(methods), scores, row.names = NULL)
})
baseline <- data.frame(method = "baseline", t(round(evaluate(base, tr), 3)))
rbind(res, baseline)
```

## Number of terms

With the 13-term library the sparse model has little room to reduce complexity. Adding products of drivers (`pairs = TRUE`, 37 terms) gives a larger dictionary:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
Theta2 <- make_library(drv, pairs = TRUE)
gram2 <- gram_stats(Theta2, tr)

ks <- c(6, 8, 12, 16, 20, 30, 37)
rmse_k <- function(k) {
  evaluate(cv_blocked(Theta2, tr, gram2, fit_ssr, k = k)$pred, tr)[[1]]
}
rk <- cached("rmse_vs_k_pairs.rds",
             data.frame(k = ks, rmse = sapply(ks, rmse_k)))
```
